text:
**My pick: XTAR VC4SL.** It's the best all-around 18650 charger in these results.

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL (4 bays, USB-C)**
- It has four independent bays and charges Li-ion from 10440 up to 32650, plus NiMH/NiCd. The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance per cell. [Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/) rated it 4.3/5.
- You can set the current from 0.25A to 3A. With a QC3.0 power supply, one reviewer charged 4 cells at 1A each, 2 at 2A, or 1 at 3A ([Stephen Knight](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl)).
- Slots fit protected 21700s (about 79.5mm).
- VoltRated also recommends it for 18650/21700 users ([VoltRated](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)).
- Downsides: it doesn't charge LiFePO4, the included cable is modest, and it's a bit bulky. A QC3.0 wall adapter may not be included, so check before buying.
- Reviews: [1Lumen](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/). I didn't get a retailer link or current price for it, so check the price at a reputable seller.

**Fastest: Nitecore UMS4 (4 bays, USB-C)**
- It delivers up to 3A in a single slot, or 1A each across all four with QC input.
- It supports LiFePO4 and has Li-ion restoration, overtime and short-circuit protection, and a battery health readout. Certifications are RoHS, CE, FCC and CEC.
- Smashing Robotics picked it as the best for speed ([review](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/)). Specs are on [Nitecore's product page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4). I didn't get a price for it either.

**Budget: Tenergy TN270, $18.99**
- It's a simple two-bay wall charger for 18650, 18500 and 14500 cells, with reverse-polarity detection and a 12-month warranty.
- It charges at only 500mA per slot, so a 3,000mAh cell takes about 6–7 hours. It has no USB input.
- [Buy at Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Their price was checked on 2026-10-21, so confirm it at checkout.

**What to look for:** Independent bays (not paired) matter most, followed by proper CC/CV termination at 4.2V and a charge current matched to the cell. Slower charging is gentler on battery life ([VoltRated](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)). Avoid no-name Amazon listings with no safety certifications.

If you tell me how many cells you charge and whether you need speed, I can narrow this to one.
